summary: A humorous overview of popular esports titles and their communities, covering battle royale, MOBA, tactical shooter, vehicular soccer, hero shooter and MMORPG games. For each game it describes a (largely fictional, comedic) tournament, a quirky pro player, and the culture around the game. It closes by praising the kinship and diversity of virtual gaming communities.
one_line: A tongue-in-cheek tour of major esports games, their made-up tournaments, quirky pro players and the communities around them.
key_facts: The 'Apex Predator World Series' for Apex Legends was held on October 13th, headlined by 'NinjaThumb', who has his own line of gaming thumb supports.
Fortnite introduced 'The Fortnite Follies' on November 22nd, along with a victory-shimmy emote dubbed the 'Shake-nBake'.
'League of Extraordinary Clickers' is described as not an official event; it had a showdown on September 17th with 'PwnyPants' top-laning his way into meme-dom.
'The Ancient Annihilators' DOTA 2 tournament took place on December 4th; pro player 'SleepyMagi' supposedly slept a full eight hours during a single match.
'The Defuse-a-Palooza' CS:GO event on September 29th saw 'BoomHeadshot' throw the match by defusing his bedroom instead of the bomb after misheard his mom.
Rainbow Six Siege's 'Sledgehammer Slamboree' took place on October 26th and cemented 'FatalFlank' as a pro who can hit everyone except the enemy.
Rocket League hosted 'The Turbo Cup' on November 8th, with 'TurboTaco' and 'BoostBeast' facing off.
Overwatch's 'The Overtime Odyssey' occurred on December 12th, with 'ZealousZenyatta' hovering by the payload.
'The Battle for AzerothButBigger' for World of Warcraft was held on September 24th, and 'SpellcasterSarah' is mocked for believing her elf is the chosen one.
The article concludes that esports communities share kinship and diversity, ending with the adage 'if you can't handle the lag, stay out of the chat.'
